web_title: 6. 12-Year Financial Forensics, Balance Sheet & Cash Conversion
book_title: Chapter 6: The Twelve-Year Ledger — Profit, Balance Sheet & Cash Forensics
question: What does Apar's 12-year audited financial record (FY15–FY26 + Sep 2026 / TTM) reveal about earnings durability, capital efficiency, leverage, and cash conversion?

epigraph.quote: A single year's financial statement is a photograph; twelve years of P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow is a motion picture of business character.
epigraph.author: Financial Forensics Principle

web_blocks.html: Apar's 12-year P&L splits into two clear eras [1]. From FY15 to FY21, sales ranged from ₹4,832 crore (FY17) to ₹7,964 crore (FY19) [1]. In COVID-hit FY21, sales ended at ₹6,388 crore, with ₹440 crore operating profit (7% OPM) and ₹160 crore net profit [1]. Starting in FY22, global grid spending and mix upgrades drove a sharp step-up. Sales rose from ₹9,317 crore (FY22) to ₹14,336 crore (FY23), ₹16,153 crore (FY24), and ₹18,581 crore (FY25) [1]. Revenue hit ₹22,902 crore in FY26 and ₹25,605 crore TTM through Q2 FY27 [1]. From FY21 to FY26, sales grew at ~29.1% a year, while net profit jumped over 6x from ₹160 crore to ₹977 crore (₹1,377 crore TTM) [1].

Margin and profit quality improved just as much. Operating Profit Margin (OPM) rose from 5%–7% pre-FY22 to 8%–10% in FY23–FY26 [1]. It then hit 11% in Q1 FY27 (₹758 crore) and 10% in Q2 FY27 (₹721 crore) [1]. TTM Operating Profit reached ₹2,426 crore, and TTM Net Profit hit ₹1,377 crore (EPS ₹338.29 vs ₹243.21 in FY26) [1]. Tax rates held steady at 25%–26% from FY22 through Q2 FY27 [1]. TTM finance costs of ₹504 crore still reflect pre-QIP acceptances [1]. As QIP funds deploy in H2 FY27, interest coverage (3.7x–4.8x EBIT/Interest in FY26–TTM) should strengthen [1][10].

web_blocks.title: 6.2 Balance Sheet Transformation: Pre-QIP vs. September 2026

web_blocks.html: The September 2026 balance sheet shows the instant impact of the August 2026 ₹2,500 crore QIP [1][15]. Equity Capital edged up from ₹40 crore to ₹42 crore (₹41.87 crore exact) [1]. Reserves jumped by ₹3,125 crore in six months, rising from ₹5,353 crore (March 2026) to ₹8,478 crore (September 2026) [1]. That combines QIP net cash with H1 FY27 profit (₹467 crore Q1 + ₹447 crore Q2 PAT) [1]. Other Liabilities—which hold payables and LC acceptances—fell from ₹7,362 crore to ₹6,755 crore, even as total assets grew from ₹13,711 crore to ₹16,289 crore [1]. Formal Borrowings stayed low at ₹1,014 crore (0.12x Equity), while CWIP rose from ₹540 crore to ₹903 crore as the ₹1,500 crore FY27 capex plan ramped up [1][19].

Over the full 12 years from FY15 to FY26, Apar generated ₹4,965 crore in cumulative Operating Cash Flow (CFO) [1]. That compares with ₹4,323 crore in cumulative Net Profit (~115% CFO/PAT conversion), proving profits turn into real cash over a cycle [1]. Single years still swing with metal prices and shipping timing [1]. FY24 saw -₹283 crore CFO (-2% CFO/EBITDA) amid a working-capital spike, then rebounded to +₹1,291 crore in FY25 (97%) and +₹968 crore in FY26 (70%) [1]. Free Cash Flow stayed positive at ₹235 crore in FY26 after ~₹733–₹737 crore of capex, lifting 12-year cumulative FCF to ₹2,299 crore [1][20].

Working-capital ratios show the core trade-off. Debtor Days stayed tight at 80–89 days (85 days in FY26), and Inventory Days held at 82–85 days (84 days in FY26) [1]. However, Days Payable fell from 172–231 days (FY21–FY23) to 137–140 days (FY24–FY26) as Apar cut supplier credit [1]. That lifted Working Capital Days from 18 days (FY23) to 43 days (FY26) [1]. Even so, ROCE held at 32% in FY26 (31.8% latest, ROE 20.3%), confirming top-tier capital efficiency [1].

web_blocks.title: FORENSIC ACCOUNTING VERDICT: CLEAN EARNINGS, WORKING-CAPITAL SENSITIVE
paragraphs: There are no red flags of aggressive revenue capitalization, phantom intangible assets, or chronic cash-flow divergence: 12-year cumulative CFO (₹4,965 Cr) exceeds cumulative PAT (₹4,323 Cr), tax rates sit cleanly at 25%–26%, and dividend payouts remain steady at 25% [1].
The sole structural watch item is working-capital absorption during rapid export/DDP expansion (Working Capital Days 43 in FY26) and normalizing finance costs post-QIP [1][10][12].

book_paragraphs: If you and I want to know whether an industrial company's recent boom is built on solid rock or accounting smoke, we do not look at one good quarter. We lay out twelve years of audited Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow statements side by side and look for cracks [1].

Look at the P&L first. Between FY15 and FY21, Apar was a ₹5,000 to ₹8,000 crore industrial workhorse earning 5% to 7% operating margins—rising briefly to 9% in FY17 before settling back to 7% during COVID [1]. Then, starting in FY22, the global grid supercycle collided with Apar's multi-year investment in HTLS conductors, E-beam cables, and U.S. qualifications. Revenue jumped from ₹9,317 crore in FY22 to ₹22,902 crore in FY26—a 29.1% five-year compound growth rate from FY21—and hit ₹25,605 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026 [1]. Even better, operating margins stepped up to 8%–10%, and jumped to 11% in Q1 FY27 (₹758 crore) and 10% in Q2 FY27 (₹721 crore), lifting TTM net profit to ₹1,377 crore and TTM EPS to ₹338.29 [1].

Now turn to the Balance Sheet, because September 2026 marks a genuine structural before-and-after moment [1]. In March 2026, Apar carried ₹5,353 crore of reserves and ₹7,362 crore of other liabilities (where LC acceptances sit) [1]. Six months later, in September 2026, reserves jumped by ₹3,125 crore to ₹8,478 crore thanks to the ₹2,500 crore QIP plus ₹914 crore of H1 FY27 net profit, while other liabilities actually fell to ₹6,755 crore even as total assets expanded to ₹16,289 crore [1][15]. Formal borrowings are tiny—just ₹1,014 crore against ₹8,520 crore of net worth—while Capital Work-in-Progress climbed from ₹540 crore to ₹903 crore as new cable and conductor lines are built [1].

Finally, check the Cash Flow statement—the ultimate lie detector. Add up all twelve years of Operating Cash Flow from FY15 through FY26: ₹4,965 crore [1]. Add up all twelve years of Net Profit over that exact same span: ₹4,323 crore [1]. That 115% cumulative cash conversion tells you and me that Apar's profits are real, collectable cash. Even after funding every rupee of capex over those twelve years, Apar generated ₹2,299 crore of cumulative Free Cash Flow [1]. Yes, individual years swing with metal prices and shipping—FY24 saw -₹283 crore of operating cash flow before FY25 roared back with +₹1,291 crore and FY26 delivered +₹968 crore—but over the cycle, the cash shows up [1].

With Debtor Days steady at 85, Inventory Days at 84, a clean 25% effective tax rate, and ROCE holding at 32% in FY26 (31.8% latest, ROE 20.3%), Apar passes our forensic audit cleanly [1]. The only number you and I need to keep on our dashboard is Working Capital Days—currently 43 days, up from 18 days in FY23—to make sure U.S. DDP transit delays do not quietly trap cash as the business scales past ₹25,000 crore [1][12].

book_subsections.title: Why 12-Year Cumulative Cash Conversion Matters
paragraphs: In a metal-converting business, single-year CFO is easily distorted by March 31 copper prices or container ship schedules [12]. Comparing twelve-year cumulative CFO (₹4,965 crore) against cumulative PAT (₹4,323 crore) strips out those year-end timing accidents [1].
Combined with a consistent 25% dividend payout and a post-QIP net worth above ₹8,500 crore, Apar enters its ₹1,500 crore FY27 capex phase from a position of genuine balance-sheet strength [1][19].

book_subsections.title: Quarterly Momentum Entering H2 FY27
paragraphs: Look at the quarterly cadence in Screener: sales stepped up from ₹5,104 crore in Q1 FY26 and ₹5,715 crore in Q2 FY26 to ₹6,591 crore in Q1 FY27 and ₹6,931 crore in Q2 FY27 (+21% YoY), even with ₹800 crore of U.S. DDP shipments still in transit at quarter-end [1][12].

Net profit nearly doubled YoY in both Q1 FY27 (₹467 crore vs ₹263 crore) and Q2 FY27 (₹447 crore vs ₹252 crore), proving that operating leverage in premium conductors and E-beam cables is flowing cleanly to the bottom line [1].

book_subsections.title: Separating Real Cash Compounding from Working-Capital Optics
paragraphs: A superficial glance at any fast-growing industrial’s income statement can fool you if you never open the cash flow and balance sheet tabs. Between FY15 and FY26, Apar Industries compounded consolidated revenue from roughly ₹5,120 Cr to ₹22,902 Cr and net profit from under ₹50 Cr to ₹977 Cr. The critical forensic test is whether that accounting profit actually showed up in the bank. Across that twelve-year span, cumulative Cash Flow from Operations totaled ₹4,965 Cr against cumulative Net Profit of ₹4,323 Cr—a ~115% cash conversion ratio. In a capital-goods business where inventory and receivables naturally expand with growth, converting more than 100% of cumulative earnings into operating cash is a rare hallmark of discipline.

Equally important is how Apar financed its working capital. Historically, the company relied heavily on non-fund-based Letter of Credit (LC) acceptances—which stood at ₹4,079 Cr in FY25—to fund imported base oils and copper/aluminium rods, creating high interest/LC charges that Screener’s automated screens flagged as a cost-of-borrowing watch item. The August 2026 ₹2,500 Cr QIP fundamentally altered that equation: shareholders’ reserves jumped from ₹5,353 Cr in March 2026 to ₹8,478 Cr in September 2026, reducing reliance on costly acceptances and lifting return on capital employed to 31.8%.

As a result, the -2.34% change in promoter shareholding during Q2 FY27—from 57.76% to 55.42%—was purely mechanical dilution from issuing 16,88,618 new QIP shares to institutional investors, not insider selling. That distinction is why forensic accounting always beats headline scanning.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Twelve years of audited numbers leave very little ambiguity: Apar has compounded sales nearly 4.5x since FY15 without sacrificing ROCE (32%), without starving capex, and with 115% cumulative net-profit-to-CFO conversion. The August 2026 QIP simply gave a high-return operating engine the permanent equity chassis it always needed.
